clue.text: Fight to send packing walker's pack

blocks.note: a ruck is a scrum or brawl
to sack someone is to send them packing, dismiss them

explanation.surface: A hiker's kit and a scuffle over getting rid of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to send packing' is all one piece, not a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack is the bag a hiker carries on the back.

clue.text: Animal ran around cricket club with ducks

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first word is wrapped about what follows

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for cricket club
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so two ducks are two O's

explanation.surface: A creature scampering round a cricket ground full of waterfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: Ducks look like birds in the cricket scene, but a duck is a batter's score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: The raccoon is a ringtailed North American mammal, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Bed frame

blocks.note: first meaning: a sofa or bed to lie on
second meaning: to express words in a particular way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed frame' reads as one piece of furniture, but it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word is a sofa or bed; as a verb it means to phrase or put into words.

clue.text: Fuss with clues rewritten, about 100 achieving results

indicators.note: something rewritten has its letters put down again in a new form
about here means placed around, so the jumbled letters wrap around the number

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A setter fussing over rewritten clues until they finally work.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of fuss and clues go around the extra C, which sits next to the other C.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone successful is getting results, achieving what they set out to do.

clue.text: Conservative heads routine church support

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for Conservative
a rut is a dull fixed routine
standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A Tory leading the usual Sunday service at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' tells you C goes at the front of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A crutch is a prop that supports someone who cannot bear weight on a leg.

clue.text: Drug agent managed to get back cocaine

indicators.note: getting back means going backwards, so this word is written from its end

blocks.note: ran a business means managed it
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A narcotics officer recovering seized cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: Narc is American slang for a narcotics officer, an agent enforcing drug laws.

clue.text: Very old bridge, one linking capitals of Austria and Czechia

indicators.note: a link sits between two things, joining them, so this letter goes between the two capitals

blocks.note: an arch is a bridge-like span
capital letter of Austria
I is the Roman numeral for one
capital letter of Czechia

explanation.surface: An ancient bridge connecting Austria with the Czech Republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitals' sounds like Vienna and Prague, but means the initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means belonging to a much earlier period, so very old.

clue.text: Approximately half Circassian

indicators.note: half of the word means only its front five of ten letters are kept

blocks.note: the front half of this ten-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone roughly half Circassian by descent, Circassians being a people of the Caucasus.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa is the Latin word used before dates to mean about or roughly.

clue.text: Dish cousin avoids at home more than once

indicators.note: to avoid something is to leave it out, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
at home is in

explanation.surface: A dish that a cousin keeps skipping when eating at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Cousin without IN leaves COUS, and 'more than once' asks for it twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Couscous is a North African dish of steamed semolina grains.

clue.text: Cliff Wilde, perhaps not the first

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter of the name is dropped

blocks.note: Oscar Wilde is one person with this first name, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Talking of Cliff Richard and Oscar Wilde as famous names.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff and Wilde look like two celebrities, but Cliff is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a steep rocky cliff, especially in northern English place names.

clue.text: Not too fussy until the previous answer is sorted out

indicators.note: sorting out puts things into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the down answer just before this one, 7-down

explanation.surface: Someone easy-going until the last problem gets fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: The previous answer is 7-down, the down clue before this one, not 9-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uncritical means accepting things without finding fault, so not demanding.

clue.text: Chore mixing pigment for paints

indicators.note: mixing stirs things together, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The tedious job of blending pigment for an artist's paints.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown clay used as a colouring in paints.

clue.text: Canadian cheers piece of vocal music

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for Canadian
ta-ta is an informal British goodbye, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A Canadian applauding a choral performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheers is British for goodbye as well as thanks, and ta-ta is another casual farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a sung work for voices and instruments, such as Bach wrote.

clue.text: Naturist daughter is in Brazil?

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the following one

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for daughter
taken as written
a Brazil is one kind of nut, the question mark showing an example

explanation.surface: Asking whether a girl who goes naked is in Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: Brazil looks like the country, but it is the nut.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes unclothed for preference, which is just what a nudist does.

clue.text: Show pals involved in home improvements

indicators.note: something involved is tangled or complicated, so the letters get rearranged
in places the jumbled letters inside the following term

blocks.note: taken as written
DIY, do-it-yourself, is home improvement work done by the owner

explanation.surface: Friends roped into the jobs at a home-improvement show.
explanation.definitionFit: To display something is to show it, put it on view.

clue.text: Scarf returned without a fight

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
without in its old sense of outside, so the letters go around the article

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scarf handed back without any argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a fight' reads as peacefully, but without means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy brawl or disturbance, so a fight.

clue.text: The girl left short term refuge

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the last letter of the following word is dropped

blocks.note: the pronoun for a girl
standard abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl who quit a short stay in a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter is a place of safety, which is what a refuge is.

clue.text: He's to buzz around old priest

indicators.note: around means wrapped about, so the first word encloses the second

blocks.note: to hum is to buzz
Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who brought up Samuel

explanation.surface: A man who is going to buzz about an elderly cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a pronoun, but it is the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the chemical symbol of the element helium, the light gas in balloons.

clue.text: Whine about beginnings of small, tender and unsightly pimple

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the letters that follow
beginnings asks for the opening letter of each of the next words

blocks.note: to pule is to whimper or whine
opening letters of small, tender and unsightly

explanation.surface: Complaining about a small, sore, ugly spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and unsightly' looks like a description of the pimple, but its first letter is needed too.
explanation.definitionFit: A pustule is a small pus-filled swelling on the skin, a pimple.

clue.text: Cloth put down after first sign of puddle

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: opening letter of puddle
laid means put down

explanation.surface: A cloth laid down once a puddle starts to form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' tells you LAID comes after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is a woollen cloth in a tartan pattern.

clue.text: Topic covered by Rotherhithe Messenger

indicators.note: covered by means concealed inside, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A subject reported in a local paper, Rotherhithe being a district of south-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a piece of writing or talk.

clue.text: Praise extension filled with aluminium

indicators.note: something filled with an item holds it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for extension, as on a phone number
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Commending a building extension packed with aluminium.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to praise them highly, lifting them up.

clue.text: Fit last four parts of astrolabe to move round

indicators.note: the last four parts of a word are its closing letters, so only its tail is kept
moving round sends a letter from the front to the back, keeping the rest in order

blocks.note: the closing four letters of astrolabe

explanation.surface: Fitting the end pieces of an astrolabe so that it can turn.
explanation.walkthrough: An astrolabe is an old instrument for measuring the positions of stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fit for something means being capable, physically able to do it.

clue.text: Broadcast court impounding RAF plane

indicators.note: impounding means shutting something in, so the following letters go inside

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
standard abbreviation for court
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news report on a court seizing an RAF plane; the RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane is one kind of aircraft, the general term for flying machines.

clue.text: 24-hour periods are stunning, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the word goes by its sound

blocks.note: to daze someone is to stun them

explanation.surface: Remarking that whole days are said to be wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: Stunning reads as gorgeous, but it is the stun of a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A day is a span of twenty-four hours, so the plural is periods of that length.

clue.text: Person imitating bird like a thrush or robin initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
opening letters of like a thrush or robin

explanation.surface: Someone mimicking birdsong like a thrush or a robin.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrush and robin look like more birds, but only their first letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: An emulator copies or imitates someone, trying to match them.
